newsitem.title: CHINA: China oil firm says no new favours for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: China oil firm says no new favours for foreigners.

text.p: The China National Offshore Oil Corp (CNOOC) has no plans to improve the terms offered to foreign firms for cooperation in finding and exploiting oil and gas reserves, senior company officials said.
Some foreign oil companies have expressed dissatisfaction with the blocks offered by China for exploration and have complained about the conditions attached to contracts.
But CNOOC vice president Chen Bingqian said that while some international firms had been unlucky in their exploration efforts, the terms they were offered were already very lenient.

"We have already been through four rounds of bidding and the conditions (attached to deals with foreign companies) are already more lenient than they were during the first round," Chen told Reuters in an interview this week.
"I believe the bidding conditions are already very relaxed... they cannot be relaxed further," he said.
Most foreign companies involved in China's offshore oil business were satisfied with the terms they were accorded and the blocks they were allowed to prospect, Chen said.
Small and medium-sized firms had taken the place of big international companies that had withdrawn after failing to find large reserves in Chinese waters, he said. -- Beijing Newsroom
